questions.questionText:
Eight persons E, C, F, D, B, G, H, A are sitting around a circular table facing the centre in clockwise order:
E -> C -> F -> D -> B -> G -> H -> A -> (back to E).
Who is sitting diametrically opposite to E?
questions.hint: Facing centre: Left = Clockwise, Right = Anti-Clockwise. Opposite in an 8-person circle = 4 positions away.
questions.explanation: In a circular arrangement of 8 persons, the person sitting diametrically opposite is exactly 4 positions away. Counting 4 places from E gives B.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Note orientation: All persons face the centre.
Step 2: Apply the rotational rule (Left = Clockwise, Right = Anti-Clockwise).
Step 3: Count the specified displacement from E to reach B.
questions.memoryTip: Facing Inwards: Left is Clockwise (L-C), Right is Anti-Clockwise (R-AC).

questions.explanation: When facing the centre, moving to the left means moving in the clockwise direction. Counting 2 positions clockwise from G gives A.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Note orientation: All persons face the centre.
Step 2: Apply the rotational rule (Left = Clockwise, Right = Anti-Clockwise).
Step 3: Count the specified displacement from G to reach A.
questions.memoryTip: Facing Inwards: Left is Clockwise (L-C), Right is Anti-Clockwise (R-AC).

People at positions 1, 3, 5, 7 (F, E, G, H) face the CENTRE, while people at positions 2, 4, 6, 8 (C, B, A, D) face OUTSIDE.
Who is sitting to the immediate right of C?
questions.hint: First determine whether the reference person faces inside or outside before applying the turn rule.
questions.explanation: C is at an even position and faces OUTSIDE. When facing outside, the right direction is clockwise along the circle. The person one step clockwise from C is E.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Check the facing orientation of C: Outside.
Step 2: Facing outside means Right = Clockwise.
Step 3: Move one step clockwise from C to find E.
questions.memoryTip: In mixed-facing problems, always mark the individual facing arrow (In or Out) before determining left or right.
